column1: # T-MISS-2: the input ledger for a defensible Pakistani F-gas estimate
# CONSUMPTION AND IMPORTS ARE NOT ANNUAL EMISSIONS. A bank/emissions method is
# required; this file is what that method needs
# held status. Companion files: fgas_stock_screen.csv (a first stock-side
# calculation) and fgas_benchmark_consistency.csv (three tests of EDGAR's 11.54 Mt).
# NOTHING HERE IS PROMOTED INTO ANY TOTAL. 2.F remains NE in the reference inventory.

column1: domestic vs commercial split of refrigeration
column4: the bank prices the whole refrigeration stratum at one operating loss of 8 %/yr
column5: UNDP RAC inventory sub-application detail; National Ozone Unit RAC survey
column6: the difference between about 0.08 and about 1.29 Mt CO2e in 2024 for that stratum alone
column7: THE DECISIVE MISSING INPUT FOR THE ANSWER'S SIZE. IPCC Table 7.9 gives domestic refrigeration 0.1-0.5 %/yr and medium/large commercial 10-35 %/yr. One stratum cannot carry both. 8 %/yr is admissible for commercial and is 16-80x too high for domestic.

column4: HIES 2024-25 design-weighted units: 23,845,872 refrigerators, 2,182,475 deep freezers, 5,701,612 room air conditioners, 3,033,324 household cars (air coolers are EVAPORATIVE and carry no refrigerant)
column5: PBS HIES 2024-25 and 2018-19 Stata microdata Section 7, ingested as data/sectors/ippu/activity/hies_appliance_ownership.csv and already consumed by scripts/build_hfc_bank_series.py -> outputs/pakemis_hfc_bank_series.csv

column7: The stock side is BUILT: a household band of 0.191-2.423 Mt CO2e for FY2023-24, outside every total. fgas_stock_screen.csv in this directory is a second, independently parameterised run of the same method and lands inside that band (0.119-2.520, central 0.654), which is mutual corroboration between two parameter sets. Caveats on the input: households only; PBS 'validation only' release (30,123 of 35,792 designed households); no published weighted household count to verify the 40.1 M frame against.

column4: IPCC Table 7.9 lifetimes: domestic refrigeration 12-20 y, mobile A/C 9-16 y, residential A/C 10-20 y, chillers 15-30 y. The bank applies flat RETIRE_FRACTION tokens of 0.067 (=1/15) and 0.083 (=1/12).
column5: Table 7.9 (held). Footnote 2,3: use the HIGHER value for developing countries - which would LOWER Pakistani retirement below the applied fractions.
column6: the end-of-life term, which for domestic refrigeration is where most of the charge is released (Table 7.9 allows 0-80 percent of initial charge still present at disposal)
column7: A flat 1/lifetime retirement is an exponential-decay approximation of a vintage cohort. For domestic refrigeration, where operating leakage is 0.1-0.5 %/yr, the DISPOSAL term dominates the lifetime emission - so the crude retirement assumption matters more than it looks.

column4: IPCC Table 7.9: domestic refrigeration 0.1-0.5 %/yr; stand-alone commercial 1-15; medium/large commercial 10-35; transport 15-50; industrial 7-25; chillers 2-15; residential/commercial A/C 1-10; mobile A/C 10-20

column4: IPCC Table 7.9: 0.2-1 %/yr for domestic refrigeration and residential A/C, 0.2-0.5 for mobile A/C. The bank uses 1.0 percent and 0.5 percent - the TOP of each range.
